scope.purpose: Govern stable information-container identity, deterministic naming, model and container segmentation, and identity propagation across authoring, coordination, CDE, exchange, and handover workflows.

requirements.statement: Every governed information container shall carry a clear, unique identity that remains stable regardless of file location, authoring tool, production phase, or exchange format.
Project code or project number shall provide the root project identity anchor for downstream naming structures.
Model and container naming shall define identity and shall remain conceptually distinct from suitability, reliance, revision state, CDE state, and S5 issue state.
Model breakdown shall be driven by information requirements, coordination scope, ownership boundaries, contractual/package structure, and performance constraints rather than author convenience alone.
Model segmentation shall not create duplicate authoring, obscure ownership, or create unmanaged temporary container splits.
Governed family names shall remain unique, stable, human-readable, semantically meaningful, and suitable for discoverability and QA/QC automation.
Dynamic physical or parameter states shall remain in governed type/instance data rather than being indefinitely concatenated into family identity.
S4 identity and naming shall propagate into S3 container validation, S5 coordination attribution, and S7 exchange and handover records without redefining those modules' authority.

provenance.migration_note: Primary S4 L4 source pair plus family-naming and container-breakdown micro-standards. Tool-specific naming implementations remain downstream migration evidence.
